title: Cross-Survey Parameter Transfer Validation of Energy-Flow Cosmology: DESI DR2 Parameters Applied to BOSS/eBOSS BAO Without Refitting
description: Post-hoc cross-survey validation of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) by transferring parameters calibrated on DESI DR2 BAO to independent BOSS/eBOSS BAO data without refitting. The study finds a robust chi-square improvement on BOSS DR12 (Δχ² = −7.77, k_eff = 0) that persists under whitening, eigenmode, and covariance-robustness diagnostics, supporting parameter stability across surveys without claiming a detection.
author: Morten Magnusson

EFC_Hz.description: Regime-gated modification to the expansion rate; an L2 entropy-flow contribution activates below the transition redshift z_{L1L2} with amplitude \alpha_{L2}.

BAO_DH_over_rs.description: Radial BAO distance ratio; directly sensitive to H(z) and thus to the EFC modification.

BAO_DM_over_rs.description: Transverse BAO distance ratio; integrates over H(z) and is indirectly affected by the EFC modification.

Covariance_interpolation.description: Robustness sweep interpolating between diagonal and full covariance to test sensitivity of results to off-diagonal correlations.

key_results.main_finding: DESI-DR2–calibrated EFC parameters applied to BOSS DR12 BAO reduce χ² by 7.77 relative to ΛCDM with no refitting, and the improvement is robust to multiple covariance diagnostics.

kill_criteria: KC1: Transfer failure on BOSS DR12 — Using the Planck 2018 baseline and the full published 6×6 covariance, the fixed DESI parameters (z_L1L2=1.01, alpha_L2=0.045) yield Δχ² ≥ 0 (no improvement) relative to ΛCDM; this falsifies cross-survey invariance for the L2 EFC modification.

KC2: Whitening/eigenmode misuse — In a repeat whitening/eigenmode analysis, the strongly constrained (low-λ) subspace shows Δχ²_strong ≥ 0 while any apparent gains occur only in weak (high-λ) modes; this indicates covariance exploitation rather than physical improvement and kills the claimed stability.

KC3: Covariance robustness breakdown — In the interpolation sweep C(ρ) for ρ ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}, EFC does not outperform ΛCDM for a majority of ρ values or is worse by ≥ 2 in χ² for any ρ; this negates robustness of the transfer.

KC4: eBOSS transfer failure — Applying the same fixed DESI parameters to the eBOSS BAO block results in Δχ² ≥ 0 (no improvement) under the published covariance; this contradicts cross-survey parameter stability.

KC5: Joint-fit parsimony check — In a joint BOSS+eBOSS BAO fit allowing (z_L1L2, alpha_L2) to vary, the EFC extension is disfavored by information criteria (ΔBIC ≥ 0 versus ΛCDM) or alpha_L2 is consistent with zero at ≥ 95% CL; this eliminates support for the L2 EFC term.

related_packages.role: Pre-registered EFC prediction (companion test); referenced for context

model.equation: H_EFC(z) = H_LCDM(z) * sqrt(1 + alpha_L2 * Theta(z < z_L1L2))

main_result.test: DESI DR2 -> BOSS DR12 transfer (no refit)

limitations: Improvement Δχ²=−7.77 not claimed as detection

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: Post-hoc but stringent cross-survey validation: DESI DR2–calibrated EFC parameters, frozen and transferred, deliver a robust Δχ² = −7.77 improvement over ΛCDM on BOSS DR12 BAO, surviving whitening/eigenmode and covariance-interpolation diagnostics. This supports parameter stability and argues against covariance exploitation, adding empirical weight to EFC without constituting a preregistered prediction.
graph_insights: New empirical bridge from DESI DR2 calibration node to BOSS DR12 BAO via parameter-transfer edge, with supporting edges to covariance and whitening analysis nodes.
Fills a previously empty cross-survey validation slot in the BAO subgraph, increasing connectivity between DESI and BOSS ecosystems.

page_updates.new_text: Cross-survey parameter transfer validation added: DESI DR2–calibrated EFC parameters (z_L1L2=1.01, α_L2=0.045) improve BOSS DR12 BAO χ² by 7.77 without refitting and pass whitening/eigenmode and covariance-interpolation robustness checks.
page_updates.reasoning: KC5 (monitoring) concerns generalization and robustness versus covariance/overfitting; this paper provides positive evidence without constituting a preregistered prediction.

page_updates.new_text: Evidence for cross-survey invariance: fixed DESI DR2 EFC parameters yield robust Δχ² improvement on BOSS DR12 BAO under whitening/eigenmode and covariance-interpolation diagnostics, indicating stability beyond a single survey.
page_updates.reasoning: The whitepaper’s validation section should reflect new empirical support for transfer robustness.

implicit_consequences: Reduces the likelihood that EFC’s BAO gains are covariance-tuning or dataset-specific overfitting.
Strengthens the case to prioritize the DESI DR2 full-shape RSD rapid-response pipeline since parameters show cross-survey stability on BAO.
Enables joint-survey synthesis using fixed EFC parameters for BAO blocks, improving comparability of constraints across datasets.
